featured_reviews.name: Kavita Singh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Celebrated my birthday with a food distribution drive, and it turned out to be truly meaningful. The team was supportive, well-organized, and made everything seamless.

Seeing the smiles of kids and the gratitude from hospital patients reminded me that small acts can create a big impact. Kudos to the team of We Can We Will Foundation!!! Truly inspiring work—this experience motivates me to keep giving back.

Special thanks to Pankaj, Kalam, and Vijendraji for their amazing work and constant support 🙏

featured_reviews.name: Hridaay V Shetty
featured_reviews.review_text:
My name is Vir Hriday Shetty ..I'm a Grade 8 Student in Inodai Waldorf School . In September 2025 our school initiated that Community Service should be done by all students from Grade 8 onwards . My parents did the research and they found We Can We Will foundation on the internet . I came with them and did my initiation where they explained the various programmes and charity work which is done by the Foundation. I started to Volunteer and took my first lecture for small children on 15th September.Thereon I've been volunteering in teaching and helping students with their studies and some of them with their computer projects ..the most endearing and enjoyable part of my weekly schedules were the Food Drives where I joined every weekend . It is very satisfying and I feel very proud and happy to be of help to others.
Simpal ma'am ..Kalaam Sir and all the others are extremely dedicated and committed as a team . Im glad Im part of WCWW and even after I finish my Certification hours ..I will continue to serve the underprivileged hand in hand with the foundation. Helping others at We Can We Will has also taught me lot as I'm growing up .
I would like to thank Simple Ma'am ..Kalaam sir and everyone who has guided me here.
Thank you WCWW.

featured_reviews.name: Ishita Mehta
featured_reviews.review_text: Volunteering at We Can We Will has been such a heartwarming experience! Thanks to the entire team, which is so warm and welcoming, and go beyond their role to accommodate and help. Can't help but get extremely attached to the kids, who receive such critical and important life skills at the foundation. Extremely grateful for the entire experience, looking forward to seeing whats in store next!

featured_reviews.name: Siya
featured_reviews.review_text:
Volunteering and teaching  with the We Can We Will Foundation has been such a heartwarming experience for me. It never felt like “just volunteering” — it felt like being part of something truly meaningful.  The students  here are incredibly kind and welcoming, and the energy is so positive that it instantly makes you feel comfortable. Every small task, every interaction, feels like it actually makes a difference, which is something really special.
I’m genuinely grateful for this experience. It’s not just about helping others, it’s about growing, learning, and realizing how powerful even small acts of kindness can be.

featured_reviews.name: Shipra Gupta
featured_reviews.review_text: I've been volunteering with We Can We Will Foundation for a while now, and it's honestly one of the best decisions I've made. The kids are so eager to learn and their smiles light up the whole room every time. The team and other volunteers feel like a real family—everyone is supportive, kind, and truly passionate about helping underprivileged children with education and food drives. Sessions are well-organized, whether teaching in person or joining activities, and there's a lot of freedom to contribute in ways that suit you. Every visit leaves me feeling hopeful, peaceful, and recharged. It's rewarding to see the small changes we're making together. Highly recommend if you're looking for meaningful volunteering

featured_reviews.name: Denny Samson
featured_reviews.review_text:
I am genuinely disappointed to share this experience. Even after making a donation, I continue to receive messages and WhatsApp calls almost every single day, which is simply not acceptable. I understand that charitable institutions work with good intentions and aim to serve the needy, but the approach taken to request further donations is extremely irritating, and frankly, disheartening.

What concerns me even more is that the moment I donate to one institution (Ashray for Life), another institution (Being Sevak Trust) starts contacting me within minutes. This gives the impression that multiple organizations are somehow linked or sharing donor information. On top of that, they seem to use several different mobile numbers to reach out, making the follow ups feel irritating.

I truly appreciate the work these organizations may be doing. However, PLEASE RESPECT PEOPLE’S INTERESTS AND BOUNDARIES. This kind of aggressive follow up can easily make donors feel uncomfortable and even question the legitimacy of the cause. I have personally received calls and messages from various unknown numbers, and because of this experience, I no longer feel encouraged to donate to any organization again.

I hope this feedback is taken seriously and leads to more respectful communication practices moving forward.

featured_reviews.name: Farhan Usmani
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a similar experience like some of the others with this organization. About a month ago, they reached out to me for donations. I politely informed them that I am already contributing to another cause and do not have the capacity to donate further. However, despite making this clear, they have continued to contact me repeatedly. I receive frequent calls from different numbers and daily WhatsApp messages requesting donations.

This constant follow-up feels intrusive and unprofessional. It creates unnecessary pressure and discourages genuine donors. I hope the organization reviews its outreach practices and respects individuals’ responses when they choose not to contribute further.

name: CRY - Child Rights and You | NGO in Mumbai
description:
Child Rights and You (CRY) is an Indian NGO that works towards ensuring the rights of underprivileged children in India. We have been working to ensure education, health, nutrition and safety of India's children since 1979 and have impacted over 4.7 million children.

CRY works with project partners at the grassroots level to create sustainable change for India’s children.

owner.name: CRY - Child Rights and You | NGO in Mumbai (Owner)

owner_posts.post_text:
67% of young children in India are quietly fighting a battle you can’t see.

Anaemia can limit a child’s ability to stay active, learn, and grow with confidence, often starting early and going unnoticed.

At CRY, we work with communities to change this by improving access to nutritious food, building awareness around child health, and supporting regular health check-ups, so children can grow stronger every day.

Source: Press Information Bureau, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (based on NFHS-5 data)

Every child deserves a safe childhood — a chance to learn, play, and grow without fear. The Protection of Child Rights Act and related laws aim to ensure every child in India grows up safe and educated. However, in 2025–2026 many children still face abuse, neglect, and exploitation despite legal safeguards.

What is the Protection of Child Rights Act in India?
The Protection of Child Rights Act 2005, also known as the Commission for Protection of Child Rights Act 2005, led to the establishment of the National and State Commissions for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR and SCPCRs) frameworks, which monitor and safeguard child rights. Together with laws like POCSO and the Juvenile Justice Act, it protects children from abuse, labour, and discrimination.

National Science Day 2026 arrives at a crucial moment as India advances towards Viksit Bharat 2047. Strengthening scientific temper, innovation, and inclusive STEM education is essential to prepare future-ready citizens. This day is not just commemorative, it is transformative for India’s education and research ecosystem.

About National Science Day and Its Significance
What is National Science Day? – The History and Importance of the Day
About National Science Day, it is one of India’s most important science celebrations aimed at promoting scientific thinking and innovation. Initiated in 1987, National Science Day in India highlights how science improves everyday life and drives national development through research, education, and technology adoption.

Education is crucial for child development, yet a significant divide exists between urban and rural areas in India. Urban children benefit from superior infrastructure and resources, while rural counterparts often lack access to quality education. Digital classrooms are emerging as a transformative solution to bridge this gap, providing equal learning opportunities through technology. They incorporate various digital tools for more engaging and effective teaching, benefiting students by enhancing their understanding and motivation. However, challenges such as poor connectivity and limited resources hinder implementation. Collaborative efforts from governments, NGOs, and private sectors are essential to successfully scale digital education solutions, as demonstrated by organizations like CRY India, which supports the integration of digital tools in rural schools for improved learning outcomes.

featured_reviews.name: Khyati Shahh
featured_reviews.review_text:
I reached out to Poornima a few months ago for volunteering opportunities and she told me about the orientation. I was traveling to India for a couple months so I wanted to interact with kids and give back. She spoke to me about a project called Katha since I wouldn't be here for more than 2 months and then I could do online projects. I am traveling for a week in December and one more day I am committed which I told I will adjust and get back to her. Monday and Friday are the two days they need volunteers for for this project. I never had any NGO reject a volunteers help for not being there for a week. The way she was communicating, it felt like volunteers can either travel or volunteer but can't do both. Never ever seen an NGO reject someone's help. You can assign as many people as you want since someone can't commit 100 % of the days, but you rejecting someone's help sounds very weird to me atleast. Are you really going to assign her another project like you said when she is here only for 2 months? Mention any requirements you have in your initial email so volunteers can look for NGOs that fit their schedule and requirements. I was so excited and now I am disappointed, have to look for a new NGO, and a child has to wait till I can find someone who will accept my services.
One thing I definitely learnt here without volunteering is don't be too open and honest about your schedule else you won't get opportunities to help. I am sure that could be one of the reasons many volunteers commit and then leave. If God has made an arrangement, accept it and he will work things out for you.

featured_reviews.name: Danish Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Diganta Swaraj Foundation is doing truly transformative work in rural and tribal communities across Maharashtra.
Their approach is deeply rooted in empowering people — from water conservation and livelihood creation to women’s empowerment and education. Projects like Project Ecosphere, which brought year-round water to remote villages, and large-scale tree plantations supporting sustainable agriculture, are real game changers.

What stands out is their focus on long-term impact, not just charity. Farmers are becoming self-reliant, youth are gaining digital skills, and women are leading change in their communities. The Foundation’s leadership is visionary, and their team is genuinely committed at the grassroots level.

If you're looking for an organization making a real difference with transparency and passion — Diganta Swaraj Foundation is one of the best out there. Proud to support and witness their journey!
